A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same URS research work. All 32 pages of each version, including Appendices A–L, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V2 reports original routing experiments, zero-shot generalization results, scalability evaluations, and architectural ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and supplies additional comparative result entries in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The UDR, mixed bias module, problem-conditioned parameter generators, decoding procedure, and REINFORCE training remain unchanged. Capitalization and explanatory edits do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 110 VRP variants and retain the synthetic scalability tests and CVRPLib Set-X/Set-AGS benchmarks. The five variants added to Table 15 already have experimental results elsewhere in v2, including Tables 17 and 25.

E2.justification: Table 15 newly reports MVMoE, MTPOMO, and ReLD-MTL comparisons against URS on OCVRPB, CVRPLTW, OCVRPBTW, CVRPBLTW, and OCVRPL; these specific baseline comparisons were absent from v2. RouteFinder and CaDA were already evaluated in v2, so their inclusion in the revised baseline paragraph is not another comparator addition.

E3.justification: Training budgets, instance counts, data generation, metrics, and augmentation settings are retained. V3 specifies baseline implementation details without reporting changed training or testing procedures.

E4.justification: The attention-efficiency comparison, training-problem selection experiments, and component, decoder, and adapter ablations are retained unchanged. The additional Table 15 entries are benchmark comparisons, not new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, seed summaries, error bars, or significance tests. Existing run information, including LKH3's one-run setting, is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 15 adds baseline gaps and inference times for five variants. For example, OCVRPB now shows gaps of 7.09% for MVMoE, 7.34% for MTPOMO, and 5.36% for ReLD-MTL against URS's 9.35%, already reported in v2 Tables 17 and 25. Previously reported matching results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(19), and complexity statements remain unchanged. Replacing 'constraint categories' with 'tags' does not change their definitions or introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified solver handling 110 VRP variants, including 99 unseen variants, without fine-tuning and scaling to 7000 nodes. The contributions attributed to UDR, MBM, and parameter generation retain the same meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of generalization, geometric bias, component complementarity, and decoder optimization difficulty are retained. Section 6 preserves the same limitations concerning training across differing problem complexities and extension to dynamic VRPs.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies that MTPOMO uses the implementation from Zhou et al. (2024) and that MVMoE denotes MVMoE/4E. These clarify baseline provenance and configuration; URS hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning relative to prior solvers are retained. Reference changes concern bibliographic metadata and publication updates, including the search-space-reduction paper's transition from a 2025 preprint to a 2026 publication.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and capitalization edits, describes the ten VRP categories as tags, revises the baseline paragraph and footnotes, updates references, and adds a funding acknowledgement. The section and appendix organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 15 gains a five-variant block and uses a smaller, denser layout to fit the same page. Minor caption, resource-label, footnote, and pagination changes occur elsewhere; the four figures and overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 completes Table 15's stated 44-variant comparison, where v2 displayed only 39 variants, and clarifies baseline implementation provenance. The added comparisons improve transparency, including showing ReLD-MTL's lower gaps on all five restored cases. These limited reporting gains outweigh the slightly smaller table text; the method and established results remain unchanged.
